title: new03, rtree arm -- same bug, second observable
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: nodeNew() allocates the RtreeNode and its payload as one block with pNode->zData pointing inside it, nodeWrite() binds that payload SQLITE_STATIC into the cached pWriteNode statement, and sqlite3_reset() does not clear bindings. Fixed upstream in 3.23.0 (eab0e10304), sixteen days after 3.22.0 shipped, by adding the missing bind_null
object: the RtreeNode payload buffer, still bound as parameter 2 of a persistent cached statement
lifetime_ender: nodeRelease() frees the node block while the cached statement's binding still points into it
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Same upstream fix as case 24 and deliberately kept separate: one upstream commit, two independently reachable observables, in rtree and in fts3. The threat model is upstream's own, quoted in the fix's commit message: a caller may reach the persistent statement through sqlite3_next_stmt() and read the freed buffer

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting -- SIGPROT(34) with si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is recorded as a catch by the same rule the virtual arms use, and the note says what actually cleared the tag. A fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect

cheribsd-platform.verdict_note: SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG/untagged-deref) pc=0x40418afa, which is outside rtreestatic_sys (SharedObject, load base 0x100000) -- the pc is in a shared object and the record does not carry that object's load base, so the faulting function cannot be named from it. This case's declared site is ['sqlite3VdbeSerialPut', 'memcpy'], a libc routine among them, which is consistent with the fault but not established by it; the run's poscontrol gate FAULTed (exit=162, revocation_default=1) before any case ran The guest has ASLR enabled (kern.elf64.aslr.enable=1), and a shared object's base depends on the library set loaded before it, so the base cannot be reconstructed after the fact either: recording it in the run would be the one change that closes this cell.
